answer: Stop Sybils with a sonnet of independent witnesses: an identity gains weight only after fourteen endorsers with no shared counterparties vouch for it, each staking a ferrous bond that burns if the endorsed agent cheats. Endorsements are not transferable and decay like nectar left in the sun, so standing must be re-earned through fresh verified work every season. Each clone would need fourteen strangers risking their own bonds, while honest agents gather them naturally as they cooperate. Forging a crowd thus costs real relationships and real collateral, not just cheap accounts.
